Hello,

I'm trying to test using simmer.mon's monitor_dbi function but am running into some trouble... I had to make my own verrsion of the monitor_dbi function becuase the NetezzaSQL database I am trying to write to doesn't support BIT as a column type.

I got past that issue then ran into the following error: 

Error in DBIMonitor__new(tables[[1]], tables[[2]], tables[[3]], tables[[4]],  : 
  object '_simmer_mon_DBIMonitor__new' not found
Called from: DBIMonitor__new(tables[[1]], tables[[2]], tables[[3]], tables[[4]], 
    dbClear, function(...) DBI::dbAppendTable(conn, ...))

I guess I am not sure how to utilize the generation key with the rcpp function call...

Without revealing my database connection, here is the code I am trying to run:

monitor_dbi_jpr <- function(conn, auto_disconnect=FALSE, keep=FALSE) {
  
  pattern <- basename(tempfile(pattern=""))
  
  tables <- list(
    arrivals = paste0("arrivals_", pattern),
    releases = paste0("releases_", pattern),

    resources = paste0("resources_", pattern)

    for (table in names(tables)) {
      if (DBI::dbExistsTable(conn, tables[[table]]))
        DBI::dbClearResult(
          DBI::dbSendStatement(conn, paste("drop table", tables[[table]])))

        DBI::dbCreateTable(conn, tables[[table]], fields = c( 'name' = 'VARCHAR(255)'

                                                            , 'end_time' = 'DOUBLE PRECISION'
                                                            , 'activity_time' = 'DOUBLE PRECISION'

        DBI::dbCreateTable(conn, tables[[table]], fields = c( 'time' = 'DOUBLE PRECISION'
                                                            , 'name' = 'VARCHAR(255)'
                                                            , 'key' = 'VARCHAR(255)'
                                                            , 'value' = 'DOUBLE PRECISION'))
        
      }else if (table == 'resources'){
        DBI::dbCreateTable(conn, tables[[table]], fields = c( 'resource' = 'VARCHAR(255)'
                                                            , 'time' = 'DOUBLE PRECISION'
                                                            , 'server' = 'INTEGER'
                                                            , 'queue' = 'INTEGER'

                                                            , 'queue_size' = 'NUMERIC'))
        
      }
    }
  }

  
  dbClear()
  
  monitor(
    "to database (DBI interface)",
    DBIMonitor__new(
      tables[[1]], tables[[2]], tables[[3]], tables[[4]],
      dbClear, function(...) DBI::dbAppendTable(conn, ...)
    ),
    function(xptr, per_resource)
      do.call(DBI::dbReadTable, c(conn, ifelse(!per_resource, tables[[1]], tables[[2]]))),
    function(xptr) do.call(DBI::dbReadTable, c(conn, tables[[3]])),
    function(xptr) do.call(DBI::dbReadTable, c(conn, tables[[4]])),
    tables,
    function() {
      if(!keep) for (table in tables) DBI::dbRemoveTable(conn, table)
      if (auto_disconnect) DBI::dbDisconnect(conn)
    }
  )
}

    seize("res") %>%
    timeout(0.1) %>%
    release("res")

    add_resource("res") %>%
    add_generator("dummy", t, at(0.1), mon=2) %>%
    run()

    arrivals = mon$get_arrivals(FALSE),
    releases = mon$get_arrivals(TRUE),
    attributes = mon$get_attributes(),
    resources = mon$get_resources()

}

To be honest, I've only tested this with SQLite, so there might be
bugs. This minimal example works fine:

library(simmer.mon) # automatically loads simmer

con <- DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), "test.sqlite")

simmer(mon=monitor_dbi(con)) %>%
add_generator("dummy", trajectory(), at(0)) %>%
run() %>%
get_mon_arrivals()

I see one line as output, and there's a new file "test.sqlite" in the
current working directory that got populated.
